major_risks.risk: The company may experience delays or cost problems in developing, launching and ramping production of its products, services and features, including Cybercab, Bots and new factories.

Suppliers may fail to deliver components on acceptable schedules, prices, quality and volumes, and some components are single-sourced, while 2025 US tariffs and retaliatory measures have raised supply chain costs.
major_risks.source: Item 1A, Risk Factors, p.13 and p.16

major_risks.risk: The company is highly dependent on Elon Musk, who does not devote his full time to Tesla and holds management roles at other companies, and key employees are not bound by employment agreements for a set term.

limits: Operating income is the published 'Income from operations' line (4,355). Tesla does not use the label 'Operating income'.
Net income uses the group share (3,794). Total net income including noncontrolling interests is 3,855.
Capex is shown as a positive 8,527; the cash flow statement presents it as an outflow. Free cash flow of 6,220 is calculated on that basis.

Total financial debt excludes finance leases (223), as required. It uses net carrying values (8,153), not unpaid principal (8,177). The balance-sheet debt lines include finance leases and therefore total 8,376.
Computed ratios are rounded to four decimal places.
The fact sheet relies on the financial statements and notes. Page numbers follow the printed page numbers in the report text.
Only the first risk factors are summarised; the report lists many more risks, and the three selected were chosen for their prominence in Item 1A.
The report notes that the company entered into a January 2026 agreement to invest about $2 billion in xAI; this is a post-year-end event and does not change the 2025 figures.
